title: Thermo-optic phase-shifter crosstalk in dense photonic circuits
bottleneck: Silicon lacks a strong electro-optic effect, so most silicon-photonic circuits tune phase with heaters, which are slow, power-hungry, and leak heat into neighboring waveguides. In dense photonic meshes for computing, this thermal crosstalk causes erroneous signal routing and limits how tightly components can be packed. Faster alternatives (carrier-depletion, Pockels materials) bring their own loss or integration penalties.
why_it_blocks: Thermal crosstalk caps the scale of programmable photonic processors: bigger meshes should mean more compute, but heat limits density and forces power-hungry compensation. This is a direct ceiling on photonic neural networks and optical signal processors.
current_state: Thin-film lithium niobate and other Pockels platforms offer fast, low-crosstalk modulation but lag silicon in integration density; hybrid integration strategies are the active research path. No single platform yet combines density, speed, and efficiency.
